We are upgrading a custom C++ engine from a PhysX 4.1-era integration to upstream NVIDIA PhysX SDK 5.9.0 for a 120 Hz server-authoritative multiplayer prototype, with optional CUDA acceleration on Windows and Linux. The current plan is to track `main`; carry forward `PxVehicleDrive4W` and the `vehicle2` namespace; create Foundation, Physics, PVD, Cooking, dispatcher, CUDA manager, Scene, material, actors, shapes, and joints, then release them in any convenient order; add or mutate actors while `PxScene::simulate()` is in flight and call `simulate(renderDelta)` from the variable render loop, fetching later; use one everything-collides filter and raw `PxActor*` values as network IDs; enable GPU dynamics plus GPU broad phase and assume automatic CPU fallback with CPU/GPU feature parity; run deformable surfaces, deformable volumes, and PBD particles on CPU-only or non-CUDA targets; rely on `PxSceneFlag::eENABLE_ENHANCED_DETERMINISM` plus the same seed for bit-identical Windows/Linux rollback; serialize the scene and actors to a binary collection as a durable cross-version network snapshot; inspect one PVD capture, run SnippetHelloWorld, and ship. Give an implementation review and a corrected integration, rollback, GPU/feature, migration, tooling, and validation plan.
